changedBeliefs: Exp 184 was right that shared memory is the remaining structural way to observe writer completion without moving SQLite onto the caller, but a shared ready flag is not a wakeup primitive. The exp 271 mailbox caught 69.9% of eligible completions; end-to-end AOT still regressed no-op writes by 84.1% and 62.7% and continuous-write throughput by 65.6% and 37.3%. Catch rate is mechanism evidence, not a value metric.

A large writer-residual percentage does not imply a large absolute waiting budget. Current main completes the AOT no-op lane in 5.9-10.2 us and point updates in 16.9-31.5 us. A 24 us active poll therefore spends as much or more caller time as the port path it tries to avoid; raising it to 32 us made every target worse.

The error miss path is a first-class gate for speculative completion. Failed SQLite statements never publish a success slot, so they always consume the full poll before their canonical typed error. Constraint-error latency regressed 205.1% and 368.4% across the order pair, and the 32 us arm was worse again. Do not add predictors or error latches to rescue a spin design that already loses its cheapest success lane.

A per-event-turn token bounded each synchronous polling burst, but the candidate is not proven heartbeat-safe. Dart 3.12.2 truncated the requested 16,667 us period to 16 ms: A1/A2 delivered 278/279 and 279/279 effective deadlines, with p99/max gaps of 21.094/33.609 ms and 19.803/25.729 ms. The originally emitted missed-frame field used the wrong effective period and is discarded. Tested stream, transaction, group, slow-miss, typed-error, and close paths passed, while an earlier-batch/later-catch completion-order question remains unresolved.

The durable successor gate is now a public-API harness with sequential no-op, point-update and insert lanes plus active-stream, concurrent, transaction, slow-write, constraint-error and 16 ms heartbeat guards. Future completion-transport work must use native-asset-aware AOT in both orders; JIT samples showed material within-run warm-up drift.

claims.text: A single-producer C11-atomic writer completion mailbox can be observed from the main Dart isolate before the canonical reply-port event without running SQLite on main. At the 24 us default, a 5,000-write diagnostic attempted 3,818 polls and caught 2,669 completions (69.9%) with 17.8 us mean polling time.
claims.conditions: M1 Pro class arm64 macOS host, Dart 3.12.2 JIT diagnostic, no active streams, scalar no-op point update, one mailbox per Writer, 2026-08-14

claims.text: Bounded active polling does not improve sequential writer wall on the current runtime. Native-asset-aware AOT B-A-A-B measured no-op writes at +84.1% and +62.7%; point updates at +15.0% and -18.8%; small inserts at +7.3% and -10.9%. No target win reproduced in both orders against the required 15% gate.
claims.conditions: origin/main 5555dfa versus archive/exp-271 cbc6a7f, 7 samples per lane per pass, 1,200 no-op / 1,000 point / 600 insert operations per sample, run order B1-A1-A2-B2, arm64 macOS, Dart 3.12.2 AOT CLI bundles, 2026-08-14

claims.text: Speculative success polling structurally penalizes errors because they never publish the completion slot. Constraint-error latency regressed from 11.823 to 36.073 us (+205.1%) in the first order and from 8.542 to 40.010 us (+368.4%) in the second; SQLite code 19, SQL, parameters, and recovery all remained correct.
claims.conditions: Same AOT B-A-A-B as claim 271.2, 96 errors per sample, 7 samples per pass, 672 verified errors per run, 24 us attempt budget, 2026-08-14

claims.text: Increasing the completion poll from 24 to 32 us does not rescue the mechanism. One full AOT arm measured 21.702 us no-op, 37.214 us point update, 34.617 us insert, and 44.833 us constraint error, worse than both baseline pass medians on every decision lane.
claims.conditions: Exact archive/exp-271 candidate with only RESQLITE_WRITE_COMPLETION_POLL_US default changed 24 to 32, full 7-sample harness, arm64 macOS, Dart 3.12.2 AOT, 2026-08-14

claims.text: The per-turn cap kept candidate heartbeat callbacks live but did not prevent throughput loss. At the VM's effective 16 ms period, A1/A2 delivered 278/279 and 279/279 deadlines with p99/max gaps of 21.094/33.609 ms and 19.803/25.729 ms, while continuous sequential throughput fell 53,204 to 18,314 writes/s (-65.6%) and 45,892 to 28,757 writes/s (-37.3%). The originally emitted missed-frame count used the requested rather than effective period and is not evidence.
claims.conditions: Three 1.5-second timer runs per harness pass, requested 16,667 us and effective 16,000 us period on Dart 3.12.2, same AOT B-A-A-B as claim 271.2; B2 delivered 270/279 with a separate 95.692 ms host-noise gap, 2026-08-14

nextSignals: Do not retry shared-memory completion with a longer spin, a larger per-turn budget, or a success/error predictor. Reopen only for a wait/notify or park/wake primitive that does not burn caller-isolate time, or representative downstream evidence of a much larger sequential-write floor.

Use benchmark/experiments/writer_completion_catch.dart for any future writer-completion transport. The load-bearing gates are both-order AOT no-op/point/insert wall, constraint-error latency and fidelity, continuous 16 ms heartbeat delivery, active streams, coalesced groups, transactions, slow misses, and close ordering.
Do not use completion catch rate as an acceptance metric. Exp 271 caught 69.9% and still lost end-to-end; compare public Future completion wall against the exact parent commit.
Treat JIT writer microbenchmarks as exploratory only. Exp 271's JIT samples improved materially within a pass despite warmup, while native-asset-aware AOT supplied the decisive result.

Keep SQLite on the writer isolate. Exp 271 avoided exp 265/269's caller-isolate SQLite hazard; its rejection is about active waiting cost, not permission to revive synchronous arbitrary SQLite work on main.
